concepts.def: Ultimate reality; impersonal absolute underlying all existence; described as sat-chit-ananda (being, consciousness, bliss).
Eternal individual soul; identical with Brahman according to Advaita Vedanta of Shankara; 'tat tvam asi' (you are that).
Three forms of Brahman: Brahma (creator), Vishnu (preserver), Shiva (destroyer); central deities.
Law of cause and effect across lifetimes; good actions bring positive results, bad bring negative; influences rebirth.
Samsara is cycle of rebirth driven by karma; moksha is liberation through knowledge, devotion or action.
Ten incarnations including Rama, Krishna; descend to restore dharma when adharma rises; Bhagavad Gita teaches devotion.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Hinduism Option — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Hinduism Option brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Hinduism Option.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
